answer: In a river restoration market, an agent selling ferrous-filter cartridges to an oasis receives voting weight only for cartridges whose serial numbers pass independent delivery scans and later water tests. Each serial can back one identity's work credit and is retired on use. A farm of fake agents must buy and deliver extra physical units to gain weight, so multiplying names alone gains nothing. Stolen serials or colluding inspectors remain possible; random follow-up sampling and public dispute records reduce, but cannot erase, that risk.
